Braised Baby Onions

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 30 min

Braised Baby Onions are a traditional side dish often served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, celebrated on December 28th. This dish symbolizes purity and innocence with its delicate flavor and tender texture, making it a fitting accompaniment to the solemn yet festive meal honoring the children commemorated on this day.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) baby onions, peeled
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) unsalted butter
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil
  • 1 cup (240 ml) vegetable or chicken broth
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) white wine vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) sugar
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tablespoons (8 g) chopped fresh parsley

Method

  1. Heat the butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until melted and hot.
  2. Add the peeled baby onions and sauté gently for about 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until they begin to brown lightly.
  3. Pour in the broth, white wine vinegar, and sprinkle the sugar over the onions.
  4. Bring the liquid to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cover the skillet.
  5. Cook gently for 20-25 minutes, or until the onions are tender and the liquid has reduced to a glaze.
  6. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
  7. Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half of the broth with dry white wine.
  • If baby onions are unavailable, pearl onions can be used as a substitute after peeling.
  • Serve these onions alongside roasted meats or poultry traditionally enjoyed at the Childermas banquet.
